objective: GO of 2026-11-23 from RING-IN-BALANCE-20261123-001 (direction 1), under the owner's standing authorization and his picture of cells that reproduce (G18, with G17). That study's table of swapped rules showed, without anyone predicting it, that under rations giving a new knot only enough for three places, with a short knot's joins cancelled, a part of two knots returns after two rounds beside a copy of itself, with no knot waiting. Establish what these parts are on real knots: the smallest start that is one, the copying written out round by round, whether every knot made passes the canonical knot test under both knot laws, the counts of copies by round under each treatment, which of the supplied rules the copying needs, and whether copies can end. First discriminator: the knot test at every birth of the copying cycle. Stop at a verdict on each frozen prediction, or at the first knot that fails the knot test under every such law.
status: Complete 2026-11-23 (successful; referee pending): under rations and treatments added by hand a part of two knots becomes two of the same every two rounds, at a rate set by what its short join does (doubling, the golden ratio a round, or the Pell numbers); every knot passes the knot test under both knot laws on the small starts; under the ration that always gives a fresh distinction a part copies itself in 85 to 97 percent of 3,344 small starts and no knot fails. The copies never meet again. One of ten predictions failed in part (holding with waiting jams).
title: Parts that copy themselves: what they are, whether their knots are knots, and what they need
